spatial_claims.claim: ABCDE is a convex equilateral pentagon with AB = BC = CD = DE = EA; diagonals from any vertex fall within the interior angle at that vertex
Triangles ABC and DCB are congruent by SAS (AB=DC, BC common, angle ABC = angle DCB), giving AC = DB
Triangles ACD and DBA are congruent by SSS (CD=BA, DA common, AC=DB), giving angle CDA = angle BAD
Triangle EAD is isosceles with EA=ED, so angle EDA = angle EAD
Diagonal DA falls within angle CDE at vertex D, so angle CDE = angle CDA + angle ADE
Diagonal AD falls within angle BAE at vertex A, so angle BAE = angle BAD + angle DAE
Triangles EAB and CBA are congruent by SAS (EA=CB, AB common, angle EAB = angle CBA), giving EB = CA
Triangles EBC and CAE are congruent by SSS (BC=AE, CE common, EB=CA), giving angle BCE = angle AEC
Triangle DCE is isosceles with DC=DE, so angle DCE = angle DEC
Diagonal CE falls within angle BCD at vertex C, so angle BCD = angle BCE + angle ECD
Diagonal EC falls within angle AED at vertex E, so angle AED = angle AEC + angle CED
Triangles EAB and EDC are congruent by SAS (EA=ED, AB=DC, angle EAB = angle EDC), giving EB = EC and angle EBA = angle ECD
Triangle EBC is isosceles with EB=EC, so angle EBC = angle ECB
Diagonal BE falls within angle ABC at vertex B, so angle ABC = angle ABE + angle EBC
Diagonal CE falls within angle BCD at vertex C, so angle BCD = angle DCE + angle ECB

configuration_map: Convex equilateral pentagon ABCDE with vertices in cyclic order. At each vertex, the ray ordering from that vertex into the pentagon interior is determined by convexity: at D the order is DC, DB, DA, DE; at A it is AB, AC, AD, AE; at C it is CB, CA, CE, CD; at E it is EA, EB, EC, ED; at B it is BA, BE, BD, BC. Every diagonal from a vertex lies strictly within the interior angle at that vertex, which validates all angle decompositions used in the proof. The proof constructs diagonals AC, BD, AD (first case) and EB, EC (both cases) but no auxiliary points outside the pentagon or intersection points of diagonals. All triangle congruences use sides of the pentagon, the common diagonal segments, and previously established equal segments.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The six angle decomposition claims (Steps 6, 10, 15) each assert that a diagonal falls within an interior angle of the convex pentagon, which is guaranteed by convexity. The ray orderings at each vertex confirm every additive decomposition is valid. All triangle congruences use correct side-angle correspondences. The proof takes a different path from Heath (using SSS via I.8 instead of Heath's diagonal intersection point F and I.6) but introduces no spatial contradictions.
